content:
Let's focus on a very concrete example: a coffee mug and a donut (torus). In topology, these two are considered the same shape because you can imagine deforming the mug’s body into the donut shape without tearing or gluing. The mug’s handle corresponds to the donut’s hole.

What counts as the same shape here is the ability to stretch, bend, or squash one object into the other continuously, without cutting or attaching new parts. So, a sphere (like a basketball) is not the same shape as a donut because the sphere has no hole to deform into the donut’s hole.

The key is that “same shape” means “can be continuously deformed into each other without breaking or attaching.” This is called a homeomorphism in topology.

Would you like to explore why holes matter so much in this notion of sameness?
